result:
I'll write about the particular quiet of a library at closing time.

The lights don't all go off at once. They dim in sections, like someone turning down a dial very slowly, and for a few minutes there's this strange half-light where the stacks look deeper, more mysterious, as if the books themselves are settling in for the night. The librarians move through with their carts, whispering, and there's a sound to it—the soft *shhh* of a book being slid back into place, the rubber wheels of the cart on linoleum, someone coughing into their elbow.

I used to work at one, briefly, in college. I was supposed to be shelving returns in the basement, but I kept finding excuses to come upstairs. There's something about the end of the day in a library that feels like a held breath. All day long, people have been coming and going, asking questions, needing things, the building full of small urgencies. Then suddenly it's just you and the books and the particular silence of a place that has been *used* all day. The chairs are slightly warm. The computers are still glowing, waiting.

I remember a woman who came in every Thursday at 4:47, always the same thing: she'd take a book from the new releases shelf, read the first page standing right there, then put it back and leave. Never checked anything out. Never sat down. Just that one page, that one moment of possibility, then gone. I never asked her about it. I think she would have been startled to be noticed.

The last person out is always the one who makes you lock the door behind them. There's a small ceremony to it—the key, the alarm, the way the building seems to exhale as the climate control shifts to night mode. You stand on the sidewalk and the windows are dark now, or nearly, and you can see your own reflection superimposed over all those spines, all those stories, and for a second you're inside and outside at once.

I don't go to libraries much anymore. I read on a screen, like everyone else, scrolling past things I'll forget by morning. But I miss that particular silence. The way a building full of human longing could feel so peaceful at the end of the day. The way the books seemed to be waiting, patient and wordless, for whoever would come back tomorrow.
